inputs.text: The “anti-corruption” label is doing a lot of work here. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. That looks less like a neutral cleanup effort than a way for an outside institution to help shape the country’s rules—and wrap that influence in language few people would dare question.
